events.title: Supreme Court denies application in Akerman v. MSPB
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied Martin Akerman's application to suspend the effect of the denial of his petition for a writ of certiorari. The application was initially addressed to Justice Kavanaugh and referred to the full Court. This decision means that the lower court's ruling stands, and Akerman's case will not be heard by the Supreme Court.
events.why_relevant: The denial of certiorari applications affects the finality of lower court decisions and the scope of issues the Supreme Court chooses to address.

events.title: Supreme Court denies in forma pauperis in Caballero-Coto v. Garland
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied Sandra Caballero-Coto's motion for leave to proceed in forma pauperis, requiring her to pay the docketing fee and submit a compliant petition by February 11, 2025. This decision affects her ability to proceed without the financial burden of court fees.
events.why_relevant: Denials of in forma pauperis status can impact access to the courts for individuals unable to afford filing fees.

events.title: Supreme Court denies injunctive relief in Ahmad v. Day
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied Mahfooz Ahmad's application for injunctive relief, which was addressed to The Chief Justice and referred to the full Court. This denial means that the relief sought by Ahmad will not be granted, and the lower court's decision remains in effect.
events.why_relevant: The order is relevant as an official Supreme Court procedural action in a pending case.

events.title: Supreme Court grants certiorari in Andrew v. White
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted Brenda Evers Andrew's petition for certiorari, vacated the lower court's judgment, and remanded the case for further proceedings. The Court found that the Tenth Circuit erred in its application of due process principles regarding the admission of prejudicial evidence at Andrew's trial.
events.why_relevant: The decision underscores the importance of due process protections against the admission of unduly prejudicial evidence in criminal trials.

events.title: Supreme Court grants motion in Clark v. Colorado
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted Reginald K. Clark's motion for leave to file a petition for a writ of certiorari under seal with redacted copies for the public record. This allows Clark to proceed with his petition while keeping certain sensitive information confidential.
events.why_relevant: Granting motions to file under seal can protect sensitive information while allowing legal proceedings to continue.

events.title: Supreme Court grants motion in EPA v. Calumet Shreveport
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted a joint motion for leave to file the joint appendix under seal in the case of EPA v. Calumet Shreveport Refining. This decision allows the parties to submit necessary documents while keeping certain details confidential.
events.why_relevant: Sealing documents in court cases can protect proprietary or sensitive information while ensuring that the case can proceed.

events.title: Supreme Court releases opinion in Andrew v. White (23-6573)
events.summary: The Supreme Court released an official slip opinion in Andrew v. White. Docket number(s): 23-6573.
events.why_relevant: The Supreme Court's official opinion in Andrew v. White is a primary legal source. Supreme Court opinions can define binding national law and alter the legal position of the executive branch, federal agencies, states, litigants, and democratic institutions.

events.title: Stay of Mandate in Steven Aiello, et al. v. United States
events.summary: The Supreme Court, through Associate Justice Sonia Sotomayor, issued an order staying the mandate of the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit in case numbers 18-2990(L), 18-3710(Con), 18-3712(Con), 18-3715(Con), and 18-3850(Con). This stay applies to applicants Steven Aiello, Joseph Gerardi, Louis Ciminelli, and Alain Kaloyeros. The order requires a response to the application to be filed by January 29, 2025, at 5 p.m. EST.
events.why_relevant: The stay affects the enforcement of a lower court's decision, impacting the legal proceedings involving the applicants.

events.title: Certiorari Granted and Cases Consolidated in OK Charter School Board, et al. v. Drummond, Att'y Gen. of OK and St. Isidore of Seville Sch. v. Drummond, Att'y Gen. of OK
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted certiorari and consolidated the cases of OK Charter School Board, et al. v. Drummond, Att'y Gen. of OK and St. Isidore of Seville Sch. v. Drummond, Att'y Gen. of OK. A total of one hour is allotted for oral argument. Petitioners' briefs are due by March 5, 2025, the respondent's brief by March 31, 2025, and reply briefs by April 21, 2025. Justice Barrett did not participate in the consideration or decision of these petitions.
events.why_relevant: The consolidation of these cases for Supreme Court review may influence legal standards affecting charter schools and state authority.

events.title: Certiorari Granted in Laboratory Corp. of America v. Davis, Luke, et al.
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted certiorari in the case of Laboratory Corp. of America v. Davis, Luke, et al., limited to the question of whether a federal court may certify a class action under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(b)(3) when some members of the proposed class lack any Article III injury. The petitioner's brief on the merits is due by March 5, 2025, the respondents' brief by March 31, 2025, and the reply brief by April 21, 2025.
events.why_relevant: The case addresses the procedural standards for class action certification, impacting federal court practices.
